items.q: Can we do it ourselves, without Visamo?
items.a: Of course, and many couples do. But if you don't know the small details and requirements of the gradual process, it's usually harder, frustrating, and it takes longer: small mistakes lead to delays and a lot of uncertainty. Visamo helps you run a smoother process, with every document checked and every step explained.

items.q: What can we get for free?
items.a: We've been through this process ourselves, and we know how heavy it can feel. That's why we built Visamo: to give couples the smoother process we didn't have, not only the ones who pay. So for free, you get your personal document list, all the organizational features and 5 messages to the assistant.

items.q: Can Visamo tell me if my file will be rejected?
items.a: No one outside the Ministry can predict its decision. Visamo's AI checks each document against the published requirements and couples' real experience, and flags the issues that commonly get files sent back, so you can fix them before you submit instead of after months of waiting.

items.q: Does a person review our documents?
items.a: No. Visamo's checks and answers are made by AI, built on the published requirements and on the experience of many couples who went through the process. That's what makes them instant, but it isn't a human or legal review. For advice on your own case, speak with a licensed Israeli lawyer.

items.q: Is Visamo a law firm or a lawyer?
items.a: No. Visamo is organization and document-preparation software. We don't give legal advice or represent you. For advice on your specific case, speak with a licensed Israeli lawyer.

items.q: What if our case is complicated?
items.a: Then we recommend speaking with a licensed Israeli lawyer. Visamo isn't a lawyer and can't advise on your specific situation, such as a previous refusal, a hearing or an unusual status. You can still use Visamo alongside your lawyer to organize and check your documents.

items.q: Are you connected to Misrad Hapnim?
items.a: No. Visamo is independent and isn't affiliated with or endorsed by the Ministry of Interior or the Population and Immigration Authority. You submit your application yourself, through the official channels.

items.q: We got a letter from the Ministry. Should we worry?
items.a: Many letters are routine requests. Visamo's assistant can explain what a letter is usually asking for and what the common next step is. If it involves a refusal or a hearing, we'll tell you it's time to speak with a lawyer.
Only you and your partner, if you invite them. Our team can't open your documents unless you ask for support and grant access.

items.q: What if Visamo didn't give us any value?
items.a: We have a 14-day refund policy, because we don't want anyone to pay for something that didn't help. Within 14 days of purchase, send us a request through the contact form with the email you signed up with and the reason, and you'll get a full refund within 10 business days.

final.title: Don't wait months to find out something was missing.

gap.title: Why the rules on paper aren't enough
gap.intro: The Ministry publishes its requirements, but anyone who's been through the process knows they're only part of the story.

items.title: Vague on paper
items.body: Many requirements leave room for interpretation: which version of a document, how recent it must be, what exactly it should say.

items.title: Different at the counter
items.body: What clerks ask for can change over time, sometimes between one appointment and the next.

items.title: Different from branch to branch
items.body: One office may accept a document that another sends back, and some local authorities don't even know the documents they're asked to issue.

gap.footnote: Couples usually discover these gaps only after their file is sent back, and each time it can cost months.

items.title: We gathered what couples went through
items.body: Many couples who went through the process shared their experience: what they were asked for, what got their file sent back, and what finally worked.

items.title: We organized it into knowledge
items.body: We sorted every detail by document, stage and office, set it alongside the published requirements, and marked where practice differs from what's written.

items.title: We built it into Visamo's AI
items.body: The assistant and the document check both work from this knowledge, so every answer and every check reflects what couples learned, not only what's published.

about.title: Why I built Visamo
paragraphs: When my American wife and I started the gradual process, I thought the interviews would be the hard part. They weren't. The paperwork was.

Some documents we didn't even know how to get. A certificate that was valid in March had expired by our appointment in July. We waited months for a slot, only to hear “come back with the missing page,” and then waited months more for the next round. More than once, our file was sent back over something we didn't know was mandatory.

Our “system” was a folder on our computer, full of revisions. Between the rounds and the rejections, the whole process took us almost two years. I'm Israeli, I read every form in my own language, and I still felt lost. For my wife, who doesn't speak Hebrew, it was even harder.

So I built what we needed: one calm place for every document, every date and every step. Visamo can't decide anyone's case. But it makes the process smoother, with much less risk of missing something along the way. Bureaucracy shouldn't be the hardest part of building a life with the person you love.

dataPrivacy.title: How we handle your data
dataPrivacy.intro: Everything we do with your documents, and everything you can do with them.

items.plain: Your documents are locked with the same standard banks use, whether they're stored or on the move.
items.technical: AES-256 at rest with keys in a managed KMS, rotated [yearly]; TLS 1.2+ with HSTS in transit; signed, expiring download links.

items.plain: Your data is stored with Vercel, in data centers in Frankfurt, Germany.
items.technical: Hosted on Vercel, Frankfurt region (fra1), Germany. Vercel holds a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation and ISO 27001 certification, and offers a GDPR Data Processing Addendum.

items.plain: Only you and the partner you invite. Our team cannot open your documents unless you ask for help and grant access.
items.technical: Role-based access, least privilege, MFA for all staff, time-limited support access granted by the user, every access logged.

items.plain: When Visamo checks a document, it's processed only to give you that result. It's never used to train AI models.
items.technical: Contractual zero-retention and no-training terms with every provider involved in processing.

items.plain: Encrypted backups protect you from loss, and they're deleted on a fixed schedule.
items.technical: Encrypted daily backups, 30-day retention, then purged.

items.plain: Card payments go through [payment provider]. We never see or store your card number.
items.technical: PCI-DSS-compliant processor; Visamo stores only a payment token and the receipt.

items.plain: We watch for threats around the clock and will tell you promptly if your data is ever affected.
items.technical: Monitoring and alerting, a written incident-response plan, and notification to users and to the Privacy Protection Authority as Israeli law requires.

items.text: Get your whole file, every document included, as a ZIP, any time.
Removed from your file immediately and from backups within 30 days.
One button, one confirmation. Everything goes: your file, every document, chat history.
Invite or remove your partner at any time.
Off by default. Grant it for a set time when you need help.
See every signed-in device and sign any of them out.

never.title: What we will never do
items: Sell, rent or trade your data
Show you ads or share data with ad networks
Train AI models on your documents
Send anything to the Ministry on your behalf
Keep your documents after you delete them (beyond the 30-day backup window)

dataPrivacy.compliance: Visamo is designed to comply with Israel's Privacy Protection Law, 1981, including Amendment 13, and the Privacy Protection (Data Security) Regulations, 2017. If you live in the EU or UK, you also have your rights under the GDPR, including access, correction and deletion.

entryPermitApplication.description: Needed while the foreign partner is outside Israel, so they can enter for the process.

israeliAffidavit.title: Affidavit of the Israeli partner
israeliAffidavit.description: A sworn statement in the ministry's wording, that the documents are true and that you'll report any change. Signed in front of a lawyer.

foreignAffidavit.title: Affidavit of the foreign partner
foreignAffidavit.description: A sworn statement in the ministry's wording, that the documents are true and that you'll report any change. Signed in front of a lawyer.

relationshipStory.title: Letter about your relationship
relationshipStory.description: A letter signed by both of you: how and when you met, your relationship and your life together.

securityCv.title: Full CV for the security check
securityCv.description: A full history of the foreign partner's employment and life, for the security check applicants from some countries go through. Not a job CV.

israeliId.title: Teudat Zehut with its appendix
israeliId.description: The Israeli partner's ID card, with the appendix (the sefach) that lists family members.

israeliPhotos.title: Passport photos of the Israeli partner
israeliPhotos.description: Recent passport-format photos, all copies of the same photo.

foreignPassport.title: Foreign passport
foreignPassport.description: Valid for at least 2 more years, with copies of the main page, the visa pages and the border-control stamps.

foreignPhotos.title: Passport photos of the foreign partner
foreignPhotos.description: Recent passport-format photos, all copies of the same photo.

foreignStayExplanation.title: Explanation of the stay in Israel
foreignStayExplanation.description: A letter explaining how the foreign partner came to stay in Israel without a valid visa.

foreignBirthCertificate.title: Birth certificate
foreignBirthCertificate.description: The original, from the country of birth.

foreignNameChange.title: Proof of the name change
foreignNameChange.description: An official document linking the foreign partner's previous name to their current one.

marriageCertificateIsrael.title: Marriage certificate
marriageCertificateIsrael.description: The certificate from the rabbinate or religious court that married you.

marriageCertificateAbroad.title: Marriage certificate
marriageCertificateAbroad.description: The certificate from the country or authority that married you.

relationshipEvidence.title: Shared photos of you
relationshipEvidence.description: Photos of you together, showing how you met and how long you've been together. Attach at least 15 photos, arranged 9 to a page.

recommendationLetters.title: Letters of recommendation
recommendationLetters.description: Letters from family and friends about your relationship, each with a copy of the writer's ID and their contact details.

jointLivingEvidence.title: Evidence of living together
jointLivingEvidence.description: A shared lease or property, bills in both names, a joint bank account.

jointChildrenBirthCertificates.title: Birth certificates of your children together
jointChildrenBirthCertificates.description: One for each child you have together.

foreignCivilStatus.title: Proof of civil status
foreignCivilStatus.description: An official document of the foreign partner's marital status from their country, issued in the last 6 months.

foreignDivorceDecree.title: Divorce decree
foreignDivorceDecree.description: The final divorce decree of each of the foreign partner's previous marriages that ended in divorce.

foreignSpouseDeathCertificate.title: Death certificate of a previous spouse
foreignSpouseDeathCertificate.description: For each of the foreign partner's previous marriages that ended in the spouse's death.

israeliDivorceDecree.title: Divorce decree
israeliDivorceDecree.description: The final divorce decree of each of the Israeli partner's previous marriages that ended in divorce.

israeliSpouseDeathCertificate.title: Death certificate of a previous spouse
israeliSpouseDeathCertificate.description: For each of the Israeli partner's previous marriages that ended in the spouse's death.

foreignPoliceCertificate.title: Police certificate: {country}
foreignPoliceCertificate.description: A certificate of no criminal record from {country}.

housingContract.title: Lease or purchase contract
housingContract.description: The lease or purchase contract of your home in the Israeli partner's name: the original, a copy and the lease appendix.

landlordAffidavit.title: Landlord's affidavit
landlordAffidavit.description: If you rent: an affidavit from your landlord in the ministry's wording (form AS/6), that they own the home and rent it to you, who else lives there, and who pays the bills. Signed in front of a lawyer, together with a scan of the landlord's Teudat Zehut.

utilityBills.title: Bills for your home
utilityBills.description: Electricity, water, arnona and phone bills for the last 12 months, in the renter's name or the Israeli partner's.

governmentServices.title: Proof of government services
governmentServices.description: Confirmations of services you receive in Israel, such as National Insurance (Bituach Leumi), health and education.

ishurToshav.title: Municipality confirmation of your center of life
ishurToshav.description: Also called Ishur Toshav (אישור תושב): your municipality or local council's official confirmation that your center of life is in their locality.

sharedFinances.title: Shared bank account
sharedFinances.description: A joint bank account confirmation. Without one, other proof of shared money: transfers to each other, card statements with household purchases or the same delivery address, receipts for large expenses.

israeliIncomeProof.title: Salary slips of the Israeli partner

foreignIncomeProof.title: Salary slips of the foreign partner

childrenSchoolRecords.title: Children's school records
childrenSchoolRecords.description: For each child in school in Israel from age 6: a school confirmation and report cards.

childBirthCertificate.title: Children's birth certificates
childBirthCertificate.description: The original, for each child moving to Israel, listing both parents.

childPassport.title: Children's passports
childPassport.description: For each child moving to Israel, valid for at least 2 more years.

childPoliceCertificate.title: Children's police certificates
childPoliceCertificate.description: A certificate of no criminal record for each child moving to Israel who is 14 or older.

otherParentConsent.title: The other parent's consent
otherParentConsent.description: The other parent's consent to the children moving to Israel and getting Israeli status. They can give it in person at the Misrad Hapnim office, by signing the application form, or in a signed letter. The ministry also contacts them itself, and no reply within 6 months counts as an objection. To skip that wait, the other parent can sign a consent declaration at the Israeli consulate, or sign a consent in front of a local notary and have it apostilled.

otherParentAddress.title: The other parent's current address
otherParentAddress.description: An official document with the other parent's current address. The ministry writes to them to ask if they object to the move. Not needed if they live in Israel.

custodyOrder.title: Court ruling on custody or guardianship
custodyOrder.description: The original, approved by a court: a ruling or a divorce agreement giving you sole custody or guardianship of the children, or a ruling allowing you to apply for them without the other parent's consent. With a custody ruling, also proof the children actually live with you.

otherParentDeathCertificate.title: Death certificate of the other parent
otherParentDeathCertificate.description: For children whose other parent has died.

because.israeliCitizen: The Israeli partner is a citizen
because.israeliPermanentResident: The Israeli partner is a permanent resident
because.israeliLivedAbroad: The Israeli partner lived abroad in recent years
because.foreignInIsrael: The foreign partner is in Israel
because.foreignInIsraelWithoutVisa: The foreign partner is in Israel without a valid visa
because.foreignAbroad: The foreign partner is outside Israel
because.foreignLivedElsewhere: The foreign partner lived in other countries
because.foreignFromFormerUSSR: The foreign partner is from the former USSR
because.foreignNeedsSecurityCheck: The foreign partner is from a country that needs a security check
because.otherParentInvolved: The other parent has parental rights
because.otherParentCourtOrder: A court gave custody or approved the move
